title: events: fix logNeedsRotation to measure content size in bytes instead of runes
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it:
In `libpod/events/logfile.go`, `logNeedsRotation()` compares the on-disk file size (`file.Size()`, which returns bytes) against the incoming event string length to decide if the log file should be rotated:

```go
filesize := uint64(file.Size())
contentsize := uint64(len([]rune(content)))
if filesize+contentsize < limit {
    return false, nil
}
```
The problem is that len([]rune(content)) converts the string to a rune slice and counts Unicode code points rather than bytes.

- Multi-byte UTF-8 data: If an event contains multi-byte UTF-8 characters (e.g., container labels, annotations, or names), `len([]rune(content))` is smaller than the actual byte length written to disk by `writeString()`. This causes the rotation check to underestimate the total on-disk size, allowing the event log file to grow past `events_logfile_max_size` before rotation triggers.
- Unnecessary heap allocation: Casting content to []rune allocates a new slice on the heap for every single event write just to check its length.

This PR changes `contentsize` to `uint64(len(content))` to ensure byte-to-byte comparison consistency with `file.Size()` and avoid slice allocations.

## Trailing newline handling:
`writeToFile `appends a trailing `"\n"` when writing events to disk (`len(content) + 1` bytes). `contentsize` in `logNeedsRotation` does not include this 1 byte. To keep the diff minimal and avoid changing existing sizing conventions across tests, a code comment has been added documenting this pre-existing 1-byte-per-event undercount.
## Benchmark:
Added `BenchmarkLogNeedsRotation_ByteLen` (new code) and `BenchmarkLogNeedsRotation_RuneLen` (old code) in `libpod/events/logfile_test.go`. The benchmark measures the overhead on a standard event JSON payload (~512 bytes):

```text
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod/events
cpu: AMD EPYC
BenchmarkLogNeedsRotation_ByteLen-8    1000000000         0.28 ns/op        0 B/op        0 allocs/op
BenchmarkLogNeedsRotation_RuneLen-8      1490671       814.00 ns/op     2048 B/op        1 allocs/op
```
Dropping `[]rune` saves 1 heap allocation (2048 B) and ~800 ns per event write check, making `logNeedsRotation` zero-alloc and instantaneous.

Repo-wide scan for `len([]rune(`:
Ran `git grep -n "len(\[\]rune(" and` checked all `[]rune( `usages across the codebase:

- `pkg/machine/wsl/util_windows.go`: UTF-16 conversions for Windows APIs.
- `vendor/github.com/chzyer/readline/operation.go`: Slicing a `[]rune` buffer by character count for terminal prompt display.
- `golang.org/x/term`, `promptui, yaml:` Character rendering / terminal cursor navigation.

Result: No other instances of this bug pattern (using rune count for I/O / file-size limit checks) were found in the repository.

How to verify it:
Added unit test `TestLogNeedsRotationMultiByteContent` in `libpod/events/logfile_test.go `using multi-byte UTF-8 content where `runeLen < byteLen.` The test configures the threshold such that it fails (skips rotation) with the old rune count logic and passes (triggers rotation) with the fix.

```bash
go test -v ./libpod/events -run TestLogNeedsRotationMultiByteContent
go test -bench=BenchmarkLogNeedsRotation -benchmem ./libpod/events/
```
## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #29414

## Release Note:

Fixed a bug in event log file rotation where incoming event content size was calculated using Unicode rune count instead of byte length, causing delayed rotation when events contain multi-byte characters
